subject: Evidence exchange patterns for short-term retentions and SSO exemption flow
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@mednexus.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: procure@mednexus.com; gunnar.stines@mednexus.com
Date: 2026-12-07T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Short-term retention + evidence exchange question

Soojin —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re moving toward a contractual decision; a couple of legal & security items popped up during our internal risk review that I wanted to flag early:

- MedNexus requires that event logs related to PHI access be retained for 30 days only (legal limits).
- For audit requests our auditors expect a signed evidence bundle (log snapshot + manifest) delivered within 72 hours.
- We prefer the customer to hold the wrapping key (BYOK) but are open to escrow if needed.
- We use SSO via our IdP and may request an SSO-exemption flow for a small set of service accounts used in batch exports.

Can Redwood outline a recommended pattern for delivering a short-lived evidence package that meets our controls and how SSO exemptions would be handled? I attached our questionnaire.

Elena
Procurement | MedNexus
(attachment: mednexus_evidence_questions_v1.pdf)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-07T13:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Short-term retention + evidence exchange question

Soojin —

High level: achievable but a few quibbles and implementation notes:

1) Snapshot + signed manifest: we can produce a time-bound snapshot of the audit stream (logs) and compute a SHA-256 manifest that we sign with Redwood’s service signing key. That satisfies the "signed evidence bundle" ask.

2) Short retention (30d): our log pipeline already supports retention policies per-customer on Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers currently have 90-day retention minimum — we’d need a policy change or an explicit carveout to support 30d for MedNexus. Ops impact: adds a per-account retention config and additional monitoring for accidental truncation.

3) BYOK: two patterns — customer-wrapped key where they hold the KMS wrapping key (preferred) or Redwood escrow. Customer-held wrapping key is fine on Private/Dedicated (we don’t store plaintext keys). For hosted, we need to confirm KMS integrations in the region (we support AWS KMS and GCP CMEK but wrapping workflows for signed manifests require a small runtime change).

4) SSO-exempt service accounts: doable if we gate exports behind a short-lived service token minted by the control plane with audit hooks. We should not bypass IdP auth; instead provide an "export service token" tied to a dedicated principal and logged in the same audit stream. That meets MedNexus’s ask without weakening SSO.

Open questions for product: how do we expose a self-service "generate evidence snapshot" in Console / API vs requiring an SE-assisted run?

Marcus
Director, Security Engineering

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-08T09:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Short-term retention + evidence exchange question

Thanks — good notes. A product-minded proposal:

Option A (Fast, contract-friendly):
- Implement a per-account retention override for Hosted (30d) flagged as an "exception" in Console (requires product + infra change).
- Add an API endpoint: POST /v1/audit/snapshot -> returns a signed manifest + S3 export link (signed URL) valid 72 hours. Export pipeline performs automated PII hash-redaction for fields marked in schema.
- Expose an "export service token" workflow that creates a short-lived principal for batch exports; these tokens are minted by control plane after an approval step and logged to the same audit stream.

Option B (Minimal effort, initial):
- Recommend Dedicated or Private for MedNexus to meet 30d & BYOK without product changes. We provide an SE-run snapshot process (manual run, signed deliverable) and document SSO-exemption as a contractual appendix.

Trade-offs: A is repeatable and customer-self-serve but requires 3 sprint points across infra, api, console + security review. B is quicker for close but requires SE time for each request and won’t scale.

If they sign a 12-month Dedicated contract we can prioritize A as a paid roadmap item.

Lauren
Product Manager, Redwood Console

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-08T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Short-term retention + evidence exchange question

For sales context: MedNexus is in procurement cadence and price sensitive — they prefer a solution that minimizes upfront engineering risk. My read: B (Dedicated + SE-run snapshot) is probably the fastest close and matches their preference to hold the wrapping key (they asked for BYOK).

Action ask: If we commit to SE-assisted delivery for the first 90 days (including two audit bundles), I can push for a conditional 12-month Dedicated PO. If product wants to scope A, we should capture a firm delivery date and include it in the MSA appendix.

Ben
Account Exec — Strategic Health

Subject: Re: Short-term retention + evidence exchange question

Elena / Gunnar —

Thanks for the questions and the questionnaire. Quick summary and proposed next steps: 

Summary of options:
- Quick path (Recommended to close): Dedicated deployment + customer-held wrapping key (BYOK). Redwood SE will produce two signed evidence bundles during onboarding (within 72h) and document the SSO-exempt export workflow in an appendix.
- Product path (Self-serve): We’ll scope a per-account 30d retention override + POST /v1/audit/snapshot endpoint that returns signed manifests and time-limited export links. This is a product deliverable that would require a scoped timeline (we estimate 6–8 weeks to ship after prioritization).

Immediate asks for MedNexus:
1) Confirm which path you prefer (Dedicated+SE vs. prioritize product work).
2) If Dedicated: share desired contract term and KMS provider for BYOK (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK supported).
3) If Product path: would you accept an interim SE-run process for the first 90 days while we build self-serve?

I attached a one-page checklist (redwood_exchange-patterns-digest.xlsx) showing required inputs for each option. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to align.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance Programs, Redwood Inference
